text:
One: give electricity its own line in your budget, and give it a raise every year: when your municipality's increase comes in July, or Eskom's in April, add about 9% to that line. Two: watch your units, not just your rand. Write down how many units R500 buys you this month, and check again next July. Three: if your household income is low, ask your municipality whether you qualify for free basic electricity, often 50 units a month right now. Cabinet's new pricing policy (August 2026) proposes 200 to 300 units for qualifying households, but that is still a proposal.

Full guide: "How Eskom Went Broke, and What It Costs You Every Month (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
